title: What is SMPP v3.4? Complete Carrier Architecture & PDU Guide for Telecom Developers
author: NAMX Engineering & Protocol Team
excerpt: A deep architectural guide to the Short Message Peer-to-Peer (SMPP v3.4) protocol. Learn transceiver binds, sliding-window flow control, PDU commands, DCS character encoding, and DLR mapping for enterprise bulk SMS routing.
content:
1. Introduction to the SMPP v3.4 Protocol

The Short Message Peer-to-Peer (SMPP) protocol is an open, industry-standard telecommunications protocol designed by the SMS Forum to transfer SMS data between Short Message Service Centers (SMSC) and External Short Messaging Entities (ESME), such as enterprise SMS gateways and CPaaS platforms. While modern REST APIs serve transactional web apps well, SMPP remains the unshakeable global backbone for wholesale telecommunications, capable of processing upwards of 10,000 Transactions Per Second (TPS) over persistent, full-duplex TCP/IP connections.

2. Anatomy of an SMPP Session & Bind Types

Unlike HTTP, which opens and closes stateless request-response sockets, an SMPP client establishes an authenticated, long-lived binary TCP socket. The ESME sends an authentication PDU to the SMSC specifying its system_id, password, system_type, and interface_version (0x34 for v3.4).

  • Transmitter (TX - bind_transmitter 0x00000002): Dedicated exclusively to outbound message submission (submit_sm). The SMSC does not send delivery receipts over this session.
  • Receiver (RX - bind_receiver 0x00000001): Dedicated exclusively to inbound traffic reception and incoming delivery receipts (deliver_sm).
  • Transceiver (TRX - bind_transceiver 0x00000009): A bi-directional session allowing simultaneous message transmission and asynchronous DLR delivery receipt streaming over a single TCP socket. NAMX Telecom mandates Transceiver binds for optimal TCP multiplexing and connection efficiency.

3. Wire-Level Protocol Data Units (PDUs)

Every SMPP packet is encoded as a binary Protocol Data Unit (PDU) consisting of a mandatory 16-byte header followed by a command-specific body:

+----------------+----------------+----------------+----------------+
| Command Length |   Command ID   | Command Status | Sequence Number|
|    (4 Octets)  |   (4 Octets)   |   (4 Octets)   |   (4 Octets)   |
+----------------+----------------+----------------+----------------+
|                        PDU Body / TLVs                            |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+

Key commands in wholesale messaging:

  • submit_sm (0x00000004): Submits a text message containing destination MSISDN, registered sender ID, Data Coding Scheme (DCS), and message payload.
  • submit_sm_resp (0x80000004): Synchronous immediate response from the SMSC returning a unique message_id and command_status (0x00000000 for ESME_ROK).
  • deliver_sm (0x00000005): Asynchronous packet sent by the carrier to notify the ESME of final handset delivery, containing the standard DLR receipt string.
  • enquire_link (0x00000015): Heartbeat probe sent every 30 to 60 seconds to maintain firewall NAT tables and verify socket liveness.

4. Character Sets (DCS) & Concatenation (UDH)

Message encoding is controlled by the Data Coding Scheme (DCS) octet in the PDU:

  • GSM 7-bit (DCS 0x00): Standard Latin cellular alphabet allowing 160 characters per single message segment. When concatenating, 7 bytes are reserved for the User Data Header (UDH), reducing capacity to 153 characters per segment.
  • UCS-2 Unicode (DCS 0x08): 16-bit encoding required for Arabic, Chinese, Cyrillic, Hindi, Japanese, and emojis. A single segment accommodates 70 characters; multi-part segments accommodate 67 characters each.
  • User Data Header (UDH): Standard 6-byte header (05 00 03 XX YY ZZ) where XX is the message reference number, YY is total segment count, and ZZ is the current segment index.

5. Sliding Window Flow Control & Throughput Tuning

To reach speeds exceeding 5,000 TPS, high-throughput aggregators utilize sliding window flow control. Rather than waiting for a submit_sm_resp before sending the next packet, the ESME transmits up to N in-flight PDUs (the window size, typically 16 to 64). If the window fills, transmission pauses until acknowledgements clear the buffer, preventing socket congestion while saturating network bandwidth.

title: A2P vs P2P SMS Routing
author: NAMX Routing & Carrier Peering Desk
excerpt: A master guide analyzing the architectural, commercial, and regulatory differences between Application-to-Person (A2P) and Person-to-Person (P2P) messaging, SS7 carrier firewalls, and GSMA AA.19 billing standards.
content:
1. The Two Worlds of Telecommunication Traffic

In wholesale telecommunications, mobile messaging is strictly divided into two distinct regulatory, commercial, and operational categories: Application-to-Person (A2P) and Person-to-Person (P2P). Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) apply radically different tariffs, firewall heuristics, and quality-of-service parameters to each traffic stream.

2. Application-to-Person (A2P) Messaging

A2P encompasses all automated commercial messaging generated by software platforms, banks, e-commerce retailers, and CPaaS gateways. Typical use cases include:

  • Time-critical two-factor authentication (2FA) OTP verification codes.
  • Transactional banking alerts, fraud warnings, and delivery tracking updates.
  • Enterprise customer notifications, appointment reminders, and broadcast marketing.

MNOs treat A2P as a high-margin revenue stream. Consequently, carrier networks deploy intelligent SS7/SIGTRAN signaling firewalls to detect and block commercial traffic attempting to masquerade as peer-to-peer messages (gray routes).

3. Person-to-Person (P2P) Hubbing & Bilateral Clearing

P2P traffic represents organic, conversational text messaging sent between two human subscribers on retail mobile SIM cards. Wholesale P2P routing primarily involves international roaming exchange and bilateral operator clearing. Governed by GSMA AA.19 standards, MNOs and international transit carriers engage in periodic traffic swaps and settlement based on net minute and message counts.

4. The Dangers of Gray Routes & SIM Farming

When low-cost aggregators attempt to terminate enterprise A2P traffic over cheap P2P consumer SIM boxes, catastrophic delivery failures occur:

  • High Latency: Messages queue on consumer radio networks, causing OTP codes to expire before reaching the user.
  • Aggressive Firewall Drops: Carrier anti-fraud heuristics identify SIM cards transmitting unnatural SMS volumes and permanently blackhole the MSISDNs.
  • Sender ID Stripping: Alphanumeric brand headers (e.g. 'CITIBANK') are stripped and replaced with random local consumer phone numbers, destroying brand trust and triggering fraud alerts.

5. NAMX Telecom Zero-Hop Direct White Routing

NAMX Telecom terminates 100% of enterprise traffic through legitimate, contractually bound Tier-1 MNO interconnects. By combining real-time Home Location Register (HLR) queries with dynamic Least-Cost Routing (LCR), our carrier gateway guarantees sub-2-second OTP delivery, 99.9% handset delivery receipts, and full regulatory compliance across 195+ countries.

title: How to Configure an Enterprise SMPP v3.4 Bind
author: NAMX Network Operations Center (NOC)
excerpt: A technical step-by-step tutorial for DevOps and NOC engineers on establishing, securing, and tuning a high-TPS SMPP v3.4 transceiver bind with code examples in Node.js, Python, and C++.
content:
1. Prerequisites for Establishing an SMPP Bind

To connect to the NAMX Telecom wholesale SMPP gateway, ensure your engineering team has completed the following prerequisites:

  • IP Whitelisting: Submit your static public server IPv4 addresses to the NAMX NOC. Unrecognized IPs are rejected at the edge firewall level.
  • Credentials: Obtain your designated System ID, Password, and allocated port (Standard Port 2775 or TLS Port 3550).
  • Throughput Allocation (TPS): Verify your agreed Transaction Per Second rate limit to avoid triggering carrier rate limit rejects (Status Code 0x00000058 - ESME_RTHROTTLED).

2. Connecting Over TLS 1.3 Encryption

For financial and enterprise applications, plaintext TCP transport is strictly forbidden. Establish a secure TLS socket using mutual certificate validation or strong cipher suites (AES-256-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305) to protect customer PDU payloads in transit.

3. Handshake & Authentication Flow

The client initiates the connection by transmitting a bind_transceiver PDU:

Command ID: 0x00000009 (bind_transceiver)
Sequence Number: 0x00000001
System ID: YOUR_ALLOCATED_SYSTEM_ID
Password: YOUR_SECURE_PASSWORD
System Type: SMPP
Interface Version: 0x34 (SMPP v3.4)
Address TON / NPI: 0x00 / 0x00

Upon successful authentication, the NAMX gateway replies with bind_transceiver_resp (Command ID 0x80000009) with Command Status 0x00000000 (ESME_ROK).

title: Defeating Artificial Traffic Inflation (AIT) & SMS Pumping
author: NAMX Cyber & Anti-Fraud Security Wing
excerpt: Learn how fraudsters inflate enterprise 2FA verification costs through International Revenue Share Fraud (IRSF) bot attacks and how NAMX Telecom SS7 firewalls eliminate AIT traffic.
content:
1. What is Artificial Traffic Inflation (AIT)?

Artificial Traffic Inflation (AIT), also widely known as SMS Toll Fraud or SMS Pumping, is a multi-million-dollar cybercrime syndicate operation targeting enterprise web and mobile authentication forms. Fraudsters deploy automated botnets to trigger millions of one-time password (OTP) requests directed toward premium or non-standard international telephone numbering ranges.

2. How the Fraud Syndicate Operates

The mechanics of an AIT attack follow a predictable four-stage lifecycle:

  1. Number Procurement: The fraud group acquires high-cost International Revenue Share Fraud (IRSF) number ranges from unregulated or corrupt virtual telecom entities.
  2. Botnet Infiltration: Automated headless browsers attack login, sign-up, or password reset endpoints on high-traffic web applications.
  3. Traffic Burst: The target application automatically sends 2FA SMS verification codes via its bulk SMS provider to the fraudulent numbers.
  4. Revenue Split: The terminating carrier bills the sending enterprise at high international tariffs and pays out a percentage of the revenue to the fraud syndicate.

3. The Financial Impact on Global Enterprises

Enterprise SaaS, fintech, and social media platforms regularly suffer sudden balance drainages ranging from $50,000 to over $1,000,000 within a 24-hour weekend window when AIT attacks peak.

4. Carrier-Grade Prevention Measures Implemented by NAMX Telecom

NAMX Telecom deploys active, machine-learning-driven SS7 firewall heuristics to eliminate AIT traffic at the infrastructure layer:

  • High-Risk Range Filtering: Automated blocking of known unallocated, satellite, and high-risk IRSF destination corridors.
  • Velocity & Burst Detection: Algorithmic rate limiting that flags abnormal bursts of OTP requests targeting consecutive MSISDN sequences within identical carrier sub-allocations.
  • Real-Time HLR / MNP Lookup: Live verification confirming whether destination numbers belong to active, legitimate mobile subscribers rather than dormant SIM banks or virtual ranges.
  • Conversion Rate Telemetry: Monitoring the ratio of issued OTPs versus verified authentication codes to detect unverified bot traffic streams instantly.

title: The Definitive 10DLC Guide for Wholesale SMS Aggregators & Enterprises in North America
author: NAMX North American Regulatory Desk
excerpt: Everything wholesale SMS aggregators must know about 10DLC compliance in the USA
content:
1. What is A2P 10DLC?

10-Digit Long Code (10DLC) is the carrier-mandated standard for Application-to-Person (A2P) messaging in the United States and Canada. Established jointly by Tier-1 mobile network operators (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile) and overseen by the CTIA, 10DLC allows businesses to transmit sanctioned, high-volume transactional and promotional SMS traffic over standard local 10-digit phone numbers.

2. The Campaign Registry (TCR) Architecture

To broadcast SMS over 10DLC without carrier blocking, businesses must register through The Campaign Registry (TCR). Registration involves two essential components:

  • Brand Registration: Verifying the legal entity using its Employer Identification Number (EIN) or corporate tax ID. Brands undergo third-party vetting to receive a Trust Score (0 to 100).
  • Campaign Registration: Declaring the specific messaging use case (e.g. 2FA Authentication, Customer Care, Marketing, Mixed Use), message samples, opt-in disclosures, and opt-out STOP syntax.

3. Trust Scores & Carrier Throughput Tiers

A higher TCR Trust Score grants higher message throughput allocations across US carrier networks:

  • T-Mobile Daily Brand Caps: T-Mobile limits daily message volume based on Brand Tier (Low Tier: 2,000 msgs/day; Medium Tier: 40,000 msgs/day; High Tier: 200,000+ msgs/day).
  • AT&T Transaction Speeds: AT&T allocates throughput per second based on campaign classification (typically ranging from 15 TPS to 75 TPS for standard campaigns, and up to 100+ TPS for vetted shortcode migrations).
  • Verizon Volume Models: Verizon enforces filtering strictly based on campaign registration status and opt-out complaint ratios rather than daily message quotas.

4. Carrier Pass-Through Surcharges

In addition to wholesale SMS gateway termination rates, US mobile operators assess mandatory carrier pass-through surcharges for each 10DLC message segment:

  • AT&T: ~$0.002 to $0.0035 per segment.
  • Verizon: ~$0.0025 to $0.0030 per segment.
  • T-Mobile: ~$0.003 to $0.004 per segment.

Unregistered messages are subject to severe carrier penalty surcharges (up to $0.01 per message) or complete firewall blocking.

5. How NAMX Telecom Simplifies US Wholesale Termination

NAMX Telecom provides an integrated 10DLC registration desk that assists wholesale aggregators and global enterprises in registering their brands and campaigns directly with TCR. Our gateway embeds compliant campaign identifiers into SMPP PDU headers, guaranteeing maximum deliverability and zero penalty surcharges across all North American cellular corridors.
